scenario: A fine-wine exchange digitizes auction hammer prices only above $20,000. An analyst wants the average hammer price across all lots.

data.description: Only lots above $20,000 are recorded. Hammer price is Normal with known sigma $8,000.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean hammer price mu across all lots and (b) the fraction of lots recorded.
naive_answer: Average hammer price is about $23,898 because that is the exchange mean.
naive_trap: The exchange stores only high-value lots.
reasoning_trace: Using alpha≈1.2 gives mu=20000-1.2*8000=10400 and a recorded fraction near 0.1151.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(20000-mu)/8000; return mu+8000*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-23898
mu=brentq(eq,-50000,19999)
frac=norm.sf((20000-mu)/8000)
assert abs(mu-10400)<400 and abs(frac-0.1151)<0.005
